title: The one clothed in white

words.meaning: for the quieting of all obstacles

samasa.vigraha: शशिनः वर्णः इव वर्णः यस्य सः

samasa.meaning: for the calming of all obstacles

translation.literal: One should meditate on the white-clothed, all-pervading, moon-coloured, four-armed one with a serene face, for the quieting of all obstacles.
translation.readable: Think of the one dressed in white, bright as the moon, four-armed and smiling, so that every obstacle may be stilled.

meaning: A short meditation said at the very beginning, before any mantra of the rite. Its words picture a figure dressed in white, pale as the moon, with four arms and a calm, kindly face, and give the reason for remembering him: that every obstacle in what follows be quieted. The epithets do not name the deity directly — viṣṇu here can be read as a name or as ‘the one who pervades’ — and the prayoga uses the verse for Vighneśvara, the remover of obstacles: the stotrasamhita text heads the step विघ्नेश्वर-ध्यानम्. The verse is said again before the saṅkalpa for the Gāyatrī japa.
in_the_rite: Opening of the rite (step vighneśvara-dhyāna), in all three services, and again at the start of the japa (step japa-saṅkalpa). The stotrasamhita text adds the gesture: the temples are struck gently five times with the backs of the fingers.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: An anuṣṭubh (śloka) verse: two half-lines of sixteen syllables. The witnesses M and S agree letter for letter.
